confidence.rationale: Control-theory reviews consistently describe these functional components, while definitions and operationalizations of self-regulation remain heterogeneous.

limitations: The framework does not establish that all relevant comparisons are conscious or that discrepancy reduction is always adaptive.

scope.population: Humans pursuing represented behavioral or outcome goals.
scope.temporal_scope: Repeated goal pursuit in which current progress and consequences can be observed.

claims.statement: Feedback-control accounts organize self-regulation around goals, monitoring, comparison, action, and renewed input, but this organization is a theoretical framework rather than one universally established mental mechanism.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Each effect compares the source-specific monitoring intervention with its declared control.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported within studies by randomized allocation; meta-analytic transport across goals remains limited.
causal_assumptions.interference: Assumed within studies, though public reporting can introduce social interaction.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Included studies contain intervention and control conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Average difference in prespecified goal attainment between assigned progress-monitoring interventions and control conditions.

confidence.rationale: A large random-effects meta-analysis found strong effects on monitoring and a smaller effect on attainment, with heterogeneity across goals and larger effects for recorded or public outcomes.

limitations: The pooled effect does not show that monitoring is sufficient, beneficial for every goal, or effective when records are inaccurate or the goal is harmful.

boundary_conditions: The target, monitoring method, comparator, outcome, and follow-up must match an included or sufficiently similar intervention context.
scope.population: 19,951 participants represented across 138 goal-monitoring intervention studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Source-specific intervention and follow-up periods across behavioral and outcome goals.

claims.statement: Across 138 randomized studies, interventions designed to increase goal-progress monitoring increased monitoring frequency and produced a moderate average improvement in goal attainment relative to controls.
claims.temporal_ordering: Assignment to monitoring intervention precedes monitoring behavior and later goal attainment.

confidence.rationale: The meta-analysis reported mediation, but aggregate statistical mediation does not identify a person-level causal mechanism and can be affected by measurement and study-level differences.

indirect_effect.metric: meta-analytic statistical mediation by change in monitoring frequency
indirect_effect.notes: Reported across included intervention effects; not interpreted as a causal indirect effect.

limitations: Statistical mediation does not prove that monitoring frequency is the sole or causal pathway for any individual.

scope.population: Participants represented in the included goal-monitoring intervention studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Monitoring measured after intervention assignment and before or alongside attainment assessment.

claims.statement: In the Harkin et al. meta-analysis, intervention-induced changes in monitoring frequency statistically mediated the pooled effect on goal attainment.
claims.temporal_ordering: Intervention assignment preceded monitoring and attainment, but study-level aggregation and overlapping measurement windows do not establish mediator-outcome causal order.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Effects represent heterogeneous feedback interventions and cannot be treated as one uniform treatment.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported only to the extent that included study assignments and comparisons were valid.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Included effects contain a feedback and comparison condition.

claims.causal_estimand: Average source-specific performance difference following an external feedback intervention versus the study comparator.

confidence.rationale: The meta-analysis included 607 effects and documented substantial heterogeneity, while historical studies, dependence among observations, intervention diversity, and moderator uncertainty limit modern transfer.

limitations: The result does not justify giving more feedback, praising, criticizing, or making performance self-relevant without testing the specific design and outcome.

boundary_conditions: Feedback content, task, baseline skill, attentional focus, delivery, comparator, and outcome must be specified.
scope.population: Participants represented in 131 historical feedback-intervention papers.
scope.temporal_scope: Source-specific task performance following externally supplied performance information.

claims.statement: External performance-feedback interventions improved performance on average in the Kluger and DeNisi meta-analysis, but more than one third of extracted effects were negative.
claims.temporal_ordering: Feedback manipulation precedes subsequent measured performance.

confidence.rationale: Monitoring interventions support one component and feedback effects constrain the model, but the complete within-person loop and its competing conscious, habitual, emotional, and social processes have not been jointly identified.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The proposed loop is weakened when changing measured discrepancy or available response does not alter the predicted subsequent action and when competing models predict within-person sequences better.
limitations: Aggregate intervention effects do not establish one universal comparator, hierarchy, conscious error signal, or optimal persistence rule.

boundary_conditions: Goal, current state, action, consequence, timing, and competing goals are measured separately.
scope.population: Humans pursuing measurable goals across repeated opportunities for action and feedback.
scope.temporal_scope: Repeated within-person sequence from goal representation through action and renewed observation.

claims.statement: Goal pursuit may operate through repeated comparison of perceived progress with a represented standard, followed by action, environmental consequence, renewed monitoring, and possible strategy or goal revision.
claims.temporal_ordering: Goal and perceived progress precede a selected action; action precedes consequence and renewed monitoring.

evidence.design: Random-effects meta-analysis of studies randomly assigning participants to an intervention designed to promote goal-progress monitoring or a control condition.

effect.notes: Monitoring frequency d+ = 1.98, 95% CI [1.71, 2.24]; goal attainment d+ = 0.40, 95% CI [0.32, 0.48].

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 138 randomized studies, N = 19,951, monitoring and attainment effects, statistical mediation, and moderators.
limitations: Goals, interventions, measures, follow-up, publication context, and populations were heterogeneous, and public reporting may add social processes beyond monitoring.
evidence.population: 19,951 participants across 138 studies with varied behavioral and outcome goals.
evidence.summary: Increasing progress monitoring improved goal attainment on average, especially when outcomes were physically recorded or reported publicly.

evidence.design: Historical meta-analysis of externally supplied performance-feedback interventions with preliminary moderator tests of feedback-intervention theory.

effect.notes: Weighted mean d = .41; more than 38% of extracted effects were negative.

evidence.extraction_locator: Article abstract and meta-analysis results reporting 607 effect sizes, 23,663 observations, weighted mean d = .41, over 38% negative effects, and moderator analyses.
limitations: The review predates current reporting standards, combines diverse interventions and tasks, and includes multiple observations per participant.
evidence.population: 12,652 participants and 23,663 observations represented in 607 effect sizes from 131 papers.
evidence.summary: Feedback improved performance on average but frequently reduced it, contradicting a universal positive-feedback rule.

evidence.design: Aggregate statistical mediation analysis within a meta-analysis of randomized progress-monitoring interventions.

effect.metric: statistical indirect pathway through monitoring frequency
effect.notes: Reported as mediation without identification of a causal indirect effect.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting that change in monitoring frequency statistically mediated the pooled intervention effect on attainment.
limitations: Aggregate mediation, heterogeneous measures, and possible mediator-outcome confounding prevent person-level causal interpretation.
evidence.population: Participants represented in 138 goal-monitoring intervention studies.
evidence.summary: Increased monitoring frequency statistically accounted for part of the pooled association between monitoring interventions and attainment.

evidence.design: Theory review constrained by experimental meta-analytic findings on monitoring and external feedback.
evidence.extraction_locator: Theoretical review sections describing reference values, perceived input, comparison, output, and recurrent feedback, interpreted alongside the bounded monitoring and feedback meta-analyses.
limitations: Theoretical coherence and component interventions cannot substitute for temporal measurement and manipulation of the full proposed loop.
evidence.population: Humans pursuing represented goals in laboratory, applied, and clinical contexts discussed in the review.
evidence.summary: Existing findings support some components of feedback control but do not identify the complete recurrent loop as one universal within-person mechanism.

metadata.description: Separates goal standards, perceived progress, discrepancy, monitoring behavior, recorded feedback, action, attainment, interventions, and a proposed feedback-control mechanism.
metadata.title: Evidence pack for goal monitoring and self-regulation

objects.definition: Study or applied context in which a declared goal, monitoring arrangement, action, and later goal-relevant outcome are assessed over time.

dimensions.comparison: intervention or feedback condition versus declared control
dimensions.monitoring: source-specific private, recorded, digital, or public method

objects.label: Repeated goal-pursuit assessment
objects.scope: Goal-monitoring and performance-feedback studies represented by the included meta-analyses.

boundary_notes: The cycle is a modeling framework, not one directly observed mental object or one established universal mechanism.
Self-regulation includes goal selection, monitoring, action, learning, context, and possible goal revision; it is not synonymous with inhibition or willpower.
objects.definition: A theoretical organization of goal pursuit into a represented standard, perception of current progress, comparison, action, consequence, and renewed monitoring.
objects.label: Self-regulation feedback cycle

boundary_notes: A reported goal may be vague, conflicting, externally imposed, inaccessible in the current context, or unrelated to actual behavior.
objects.definition: A specified desired state, avoided state, criterion, or outcome against which current progress can be evaluated.
objects.label: Represented goal or standard

boundary_notes: Perceived progress can differ from recorded behavior or objective outcome.
objects.definition: Time-indexed estimate of the person's current position or rate of change relative to a declared goal.
objects.label: Perceived current goal progress

boundary_notes: A discrepancy is not automatically motivating; it can be ignored, misestimated, tolerated, acted on, or resolved by revising the goal.
objects.definition: Time-indexed represented difference between a goal standard and perceived current progress.
objects.label: Perceived goal-progress discrepancy

objects.definition: Observable checking, counting, recording, reviewing, or reporting of behavior or outcomes relevant to a declared goal.
objects.function_note: Monitoring creates information; it does not by itself specify a useful action or guarantee goal attainment.
objects.label: Goal-progress monitoring behavior
objects.response_topography: Source-specific self-weighing, diary entry, checklist completion, device check, performance review, or public report.

objects.definition: Observable action, response inhibition, strategy change, environmental modification, help seeking, persistence, or disengagement performed in relation to a declared goal.
objects.function_note: The same action can serve different goals, and the same goal can be pursued through different actions.
objects.label: Self-regulatory action
objects.response_topography: Prespecified goal-relevant behavior recorded in the source-specific task or daily setting.

boundary_notes: Recording can change behavior and can also be incomplete, selectively reported, or poorly aligned with the actual goal.
objects.definition: Declared behavioral or outcome record used to estimate current progress toward a specified goal.
objects.label: Recorded goal-progress measure
objects.method: Define the target behavior or outcome, unit, observation window, recording method, missing-data rule, and whether the record is private, physical, digital, or public.

boundary_notes: Attainment of a chosen goal does not establish that the goal was healthy, autonomous, optimal, or achieved by the proposed mechanism.
objects.definition: Degree to which a declared behavioral or outcome criterion is reached within a specified observation period.
objects.label: Prespecified goal attainment

objects.definition: Experimental or applied instruction, reminder, tool, or reporting requirement designed to increase the frequency of monitoring progress toward a declared goal.
objects.delivery: Source-specific prompt, diary, device, physical record, or reporting arrangement compared with a control condition.
objects.label: Goal-progress monitoring intervention

objects.definition: Information supplied by an external agent about one or more aspects of a person's task performance.
objects.delivery: Source-specific verbal, written, computerized, outcome, process, praise, discouragement, or solution information.
objects.label: External performance feedback

boundary_notes: Monitoring effects do not prove that every intervention works through a consciously represented discrepancy.
Goal conflict, habit, emotion, skill, opportunity, social context, and resource constraints can interrupt or redirect the loop.
objects.definition: Proposed process in which perceived current progress is compared with a represented goal and the resulting discrepancy helps select or revise action, after which consequences provide new input.
objects.label: Goal-discrepancy feedback control
realization_conditions: A sufficiently specified goal and goal-relevant input are available.
The person can detect or receive information about progress and has at least one available response.
Consequences can be monitored before the next comparison or goal revision.

sources.authority_note: Contemporary theoretical review used to define the feedback-control framework and its scope, not as empirical proof of the complete mechanism.
sources.title: Control theory, goal attainment, and psychopathology

sources.authority_note: Large meta-analysis of randomized progress-monitoring interventions used for bounded causal and statistical-mediation claims.
sources.title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence

sources.authority_note: Large historical meta-analysis used to prevent treating generic performance feedback as uniformly beneficial and to keep its explanatory theory provisional.
sources.title: The effects of feedback interventions on performance — a historical review, a meta-analysis, and a preliminary feedback intervention theory
